item.title: 'I'm so tired and also disappointed' - Matheus Cunha admits sitting in the relegation zone 'is not normal' after Manchester United's 4-4 thriller against Aston Villa
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United forward Matheus Cunha has expressed his exhaustion and frustration after his side twice fought back from two goals down to salvage a 4-4 home draw against Aston Villa. Despite rescuing a dramatic late point at Old Trafford on Sunday, the Red Devils enter the November international break languishing in 18th place. Brazilian forward laments slow starts Cunha played the full 90 minutes on Sunday after inspiring a midweek 3-2 Champions League comeback win over Roma , earning a 16th-minute penalty when fouled by Boubacar Kamara and testing keeper Zion Suzuki from distance. Bruno Fernandes converted that spot-kick before Youri Tielemans cancelled out early strikes from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson. After John McGinn's penalty and Leon Goretzka made it 4-2, stoppage-time goals from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu rescued a point . Late comebacks mask mentality issue Questioning why his team only show urgency after falling behind, Cunha told Sky Sports : "I'm so tired and also disappointed. After the other night [against Roma] we talked about how we concede goals and have the mentality to come back in the game. "We did it again where we had to play like Manchester United and go forward. We showed courage, but we only do this after we concede goals. "We showed character after conceding goals. If we had shown that character and courage before, then we will win more games. "I don't know why we are making it hard for ourselves. We all work hard, and we all want to be the best. We need to change our mentality from the beginning." Attacker sympathises with frustrated supporters Failing to keep a clean sheet across their opening 10 league games for the first time since 1986-87 has left United in their lowest position at this stage of a top-flight campaign since sitting 20th that same season. Understanding why the Old Trafford faithful are unhappy , Cunha added: "Before we played, everyone is a fan. You understand why they are frustrated. This is completely fine; we understand. "We are on the pitch, and we need to manage this. We need to change the mentality, be in the game. I don't think the fans are against us; it's just that they want to see us perform and win games. "Before anything else, we need to look inside to us - the players, the staff. It's a huge club and to feel something like this [being so low down in the standings] is not normal." Liverpool test awaits after hiatus Winless in eight Premier League outings to match a barren run from April to May 2025, United are now guaranteed to spend at least 15 straight days in the drop zone , their longest top-flight stretch since a 28-day spell in September and October 1986. Cunha and his team-mates must use the two-week international pause to fix their defensive flaws. Once domestic action resumes in a fortnight, the Red Devils face a daunting clash against rivals Liverpool.

item.title: MVPW07 Results: Baumgardner Defuses Turhan, Unification Fight Looming
item.description: What to Know Women’s boxing thrilled fans in Arlington, Texas and watching on ESPN at Most Valuable Promotions’ MVPW07 card on Sunday. Alycia Baumgardner took Elif Nur Turhan to the cleaners with three shutout scorecards in a dominating performance. Ramla Ali scored her biggest, while Irma Garcia and Skye Nicolson defended their titles. In Sunday’s main event on the Most Valuable Promotions MVPW07 card, Alycia Baumgardner of Detroit stepped up and showed out in her first fight as a lightweight. Alycia Baumgardner reacts to her three shutout scorecards declaring her the winner. Photo: Most Valuable Promotions “The Bomb” thoroughly defused one of boxing’s hard-punching women and our 2025 Fighter of the Year , Elif Nur Turhan of Turkey. Turhan did not win a single round on any of the three scorecards against Baumgardner, a triple 100-90 shutout. Baumgardner is now the IBF World Lightweight champion. It was the first loss for “The Golden Turkish Warrior” Turhan (14-1, 8 KOs) at the hands of Baumgardner (19-1, 7 KOs ), who has never looked more in control. “This was somebody that I was very humble to fight, and I needed this fight to keep me humble, to keep me hungry, and be the best fighter that I can be,” said Baumgardner. Baumgardner and trainer Derrick James trained hard and put together the ideal game plan against Turhan. Turhan swings for the fences, relying on her power much like a male heavyweight who can lose every round but win the fight with a single punch. They recognized that Baumgardner could neutralize her with speed, with a stinging jab and straight power shots. Baumgardner said she and James knew Turhan would come out swinging. “ We knew that’s how she comes to fight. So it was all about staying composed and staying true to what I’m great at, and that’s keeping my hands up. That’s being skillful. The skills pay the bills, baby!” Baumgardner landed more than half of her power punches thanks to her superior accuracy and counterpunching. She was well conditioned to fight three-minute rounds, saying she sparred more than 160 rounds in training camp. It paid off: her punch output increased through the fight, and she threw and landed the most punches in the final round as Turhan faded. According to CompuBox, Turhan landed an average of just five punches per round. Baumgardner landed 43% of her punches thrown in combination to just 16% for Turhan. “I was prepared for that fight, and so when I’m in there, I just think, man, I trained for this,” said Baumgardner. “This was supposed to be the fun part, and I definitely made it fun and made it exciting and entertaining, and I hope everybody was entertained tonight.” Sitting ringside watching with great interest was WBC/WBO World Lightweight champion Caroline Dubois, who will face WBA World Lightweight champion Stephanie Han to unify the rest of the titles on February 20 in El Paso . Count on a fight for undisputed between the winner and Baumgardner in the spring. Ramla Ali Wins First World Title

item.title: Footballer to help kids get their kicks outdoor
item.description: Hull City captain Lewie Coyle is encouraging children to play with a smile [Jasmine Lowe/BBC News] The captain of a Premier League team has launched a street football programme to encourage more children to enjoy outdoor play. Hull City defender Lewie Coyle said his career began by kicking a ball in an alleyway near the East Hull home where he grew up and he has called for more children to follow in his footsteps. The 31-year-old said: "I believe being allowed to lark (play) about outside gave me a head start in pursuing what my career has turned out to be as a professional footballer." Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, is backing Coyle's call: "Playing outside develops confidence, creativity, resilience and independence. It's good for physical and mental health." Coyle led his hometown club to victory in the Championship play-off final in May, securing the Tigers' promotion to the Premier League. Through the Lewie Coyle Football Academy, the defender is launching LCFA Street Football and has vowed to visit estates across the city and hold free pop-up events to encourage outdoor play among children. Coyle said his Hull City team-mates had donated as part of the campaign to ensure every child taking part received a free football. He said: "I just want to encourage kids to move again. We need kids to be kids and play on the street, but of course, in a safe environment. "I had so many amazing memories growing up on the streets of Bilton. It taught me confidence and social skills, and it was character-building. "We're in an era now where kids socialise through technology, but I think as adults we need to make sure there's more of a push for our children to play out in the same way we did. "We're going to chuck some jumpers down and use them as goalposts, and we're really going to throw it back. As it says on the tin, we're just going to have a kickabout on the streets." Scunthorpe-born Dame Rachel de Souza is backing Lewie Coyle's call for more outdoor play [PA Media] Coyle's message has been backed by de Souza, who said it echoed new research from her office that showed "boys and girls want to play outside". She said: "I've spoken to children across the nation through my Big Future survey and, from Land's End to Hadrian's Wall, I hear the same message: boys and girls want to play. "They want to be outside, be active and be with friends in places where they feel safe and welcome. "But, there are so many barriers right now, from the cost of living to a lack of places to go, especially for teenagers and disabled children. "We all need to champion play and remember that childhood can't be, and shouldn't be, completely risk-free." I’ve been saying it for weeks: Xhaka has been holding us back because his legs have gone, but lo and behold, an energetic box-to-box midfielder replaces him and we look like the Sunderland of last year! Bullish Brian Brobbey Unplayable. He would’ve been pulling Levi Colwill and Wesley Fofana out of his pockets when he got home. I just wish he could discover his shooting boots as that would’ve been a fantastic sixty five minutes for him. I do hope he’s not injured, though. A wholehearted Sunderland display We actually looked capable of defending and that was down to having Nordi Mukiele in there. Special mentions also for Thomas Meunier and Reinildo — both elder statesman, but they had the better of the Chelsea wingers they faced throughout I mentioned it above, but this was the Sunderland of last season. Why? Because they were at it from the off; determined, intense and performed as a team. Understandably, the pace dropped in the second half but the Lads still bettered their opposition. Opportunities wasted We need to be better at finishing chances. Brobbey had two and Wilson Isidor one. For such an inexperienced player, he plays with confidence and maturity. He always seems to have time and space; he passes sensibly and gets around the pitch really well. Poor finishing Why can’t we finish from extremely promising positions? We just have to take our chances — the game would’ve been over a lot earlier if we had. Jarred Gillett…oh dear Can someone explain how he has the competence to be a top level referee? It says it all that Régis Le Bris got a yellow card. John Wilson says… Sunderland’s intensity returns The word that’s been missing from our performances recently was back. The Lads (with help from the crowd) were back. Regis Le Bris made seven changes from the team that lost to Dinamo Zagreb on Thursday, with Thomas Meunier, Nordi Mukiele, Luke O’Nien, Reinildo Mandava, Le Fée, Chemsdine Talbi and Brian Brobbey coming into the starting eleven. item.title: Michael Carrick sack update: INEOS to hold crunch talks at Carrington to decide Man United head coach’s fate
item.description: Michael Carrick sack update: INEOS to hold crunch talks at Carrington to decide Man United head coach’s fate INEOS had given Michael Carrick three games to save his job. Manchester United won only one of them. However, there were promising signs nonetheless. The Red Devils were the better team in the first half against Chelsea before Lisandro Martinez threw it all away in the second 45 minutes. Then the 20-time English league champions came from two goals down to beat AS Roma in the Champions League, before producing two comebacks in either half against Aston Villa to snatch a late point. While this style of play is unsustainable , it is evident that the players are trying for the head coach , and INEOS have taken note of it. This explains why they are considering keeping the former United midfielder in charge beyond the November international break. Meeting regarding Carrick next week According to TEAMtalk , the hierarchy will conduct another meeting at Carrington early next week to sort out Carrick’s future. As things stand, Jason Wilcox is backing him to steady the ship. “I am told Manchester United’s hierarchy are due to meet at Carrington early next week, with Michael Carrick’s future very much under discussion. The meeting was already planned even before the recent fixtures. That was the plan. “They considered Carrick’s position after the Bournemouth game but did not want a long-term interim had they made a change. “Jason Wilcox now goes into the international break with a huge decision to make, as TEAMtalk has already revealed he is the Kingmaker and will ultimately decide whether Carrick stays or not. Wilcox has thus shown his backing for Carrick.” No clear alternative This stance could also be because no unanimous alternative has emerged as yet. While it emerged that Eddie Howe was the football director’s preferred choice, not everyone was in agreement. Recruitment chief Christopher Vivell wanted Julian Nagelsmann , who has since turned the opportunity down . Some within the hierarchy preferred a more ambitious name like Unai Emery or Cesc Fabregas . The Villa boss is close to signing a long-term deal at Villa Park, while the Como boss is unlikely to jump ship midseason . Antonio Conte is the other high-profile name in the running, but the Italian’s demands are unlikely to be accepted by INEOS. Feature image Dan Istitene via Getty Images online polls

item.title: OTD (09/11/1992): Crosby Is Caretaker At Sunderland… Again!
item.description: Sunderland 1-2 Leicester, League match at Roker Park, Sunday 15th November 1992. Brian Atkinson, Sunderland, gets the better of Colin Hull of Leicester. (Photo by NCJ Archive/Mirrorpix/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just six months earlier, it was probably the proudest moment in Malcolm Crosby’s footballing career as he led Sunderland out at Wembley as the manager who had taken them to the final and was ninety minutes away from becoming immortal. It wasn’t to be, as Liverpool ran out comfortable winners on the day, but then the real work was to begin. First up, his captain Paul Bracewell was fobbed off by the Sunderland board, so joined Keegan’s revolution up the road. Then Paul Hardyman had a tantrum because he was left out of the FA Cup final squad and joined Bristol Rovers. It was compounded by the fact that, after a whole host of players were linked with joining the club, only three signed to join the ranks. Shaun Cunnington from Grimsby Town, John Colquhoun from Hearts and, at weekends, Crosby’s assistant Bobby Ferguson called up his mate Terry Butcher to help us out, as his knee wouldn’t allow him to train. Things weren’t looking good to begin with, but four wins in the first 14 games confirmed everyone’s fears. It would be another season of struggle in Barclays League Division One (the Championship in new money). Two days earlier, Crosby’s Sunderland had been demolished 5-2 at Chris Turner’s Peterborough United, with the home side being 4-1 up on the hour mark. With the form the way it was, the table was looking bleak and, after a capitulation at London Road, it was looking like the end for Crosby as Sunderland manager. However, two days later, it was reported by Geoff Storey in the Sunderland Echo that Crosby would indeed be in the dugout for the next fixture at Roker Park against Leicester City. This wasn’t because the Roker boss had received a vote of confidence. It was reported “that the board had not been able to come up with a replacement that would appease disgruntled fans”. This led to comments by Aidan Semmens in the Echo, stating: “Malcolm Crosby began his career as Sunderland manager as caretaker. Now it seems he is in a caretaker’s role again”. There had been no word from chairman Bob Murray or the directors on the manager’s position, so much so that publicly Crosby believed his job was not under immediate threat: Everybody keeps going on about it, saying the board will sack me. The board has been great. They have let me get on with the job, but unfortunately we haven’t backed it up with results. Whatever decisions people make I, as a manager, have got to accept that decision. If they say enough is enough, I will have to accept that. Everybody knows that when you become a manager. I’m not worried about being sacked. What worries me is how we can play well in the two previous matches and at times play well against Peterborough, but then let goals in like we have. I’m worried about the players and I’m concerned for the supporters.

item.title: Verstappen reveals what went wrong with RB22 despite impressive charge
item.description: Max Verstappen finished second in the Brazilian Grand Prix after a superb comeback drive. Even so, he was not entirely satisfied with his pace during the race. Speaking to Viaplay , Verstappen looked back on the race at Interlagos: "After my stint on the intermediates, it actually felt really bad. I don't know what went wrong or what broke on the car, but it was basically undriveable. There was an extreme amount of oversteer in the fast corners. For example, in that final kink. You should normally be able to take it flat out, but I could barely keep it at full throttle. That was a shame, in that respect." After a superb opening phase, the Dutchman was on course for a podium finish: "We were quickly up around the podium places, but somehow something still went wrong." Verstappen then explained what the problems were. "I couldn't turn the steering wheel in the fast corners; it was really bizarre. We need to check the car, and they were able to see something. But you don't have that many sensors on the car during a race, so it has to be taken apart. It was clear that something wasn't right." Verstappen puts on a superb comeback drive Verstappen made a superb comeback during the opening phase of the race. Despite the rain, the Dutchman started in first gear, he admitted. During the laps to the grid, Verstappen felt that the car was in good shape. "On the laps to the grid, the car still felt pretty good. Then I went out and thought I had very little grip. But when I looked at the cars around me, I realized that I actually had a lot of grip," said a smiling Verstappen. Verstappen finished second in the Brazilian GP. item.title: Chicago Bears Fans Waiting All Night for Good, Better, Best
item.description: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - NOVEMBER 08: Jeffery Simmons #99 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after a sack against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the fourth quarter at Soldier Field on November 08, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by John Fisher/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the third time in three weeks, I find myself in a familiar spot. Fired up after a Chicago Bears primetime victory, I sit waiting to hear seventeen sweet words before I go to bed. “Good, better, best. Never let it rest. Until your good gets better, and your better gets best.” Carrie Underwood may have been waiting all day for Sunday night, but I’ve been waiting all night for Good, Better, Best. Doctors may frown upon screen time before bed, but I can’t sleep until I see it. For those of you Bears fans who prioritize a good night’s sleep over watching Ben Johnson give out game balls and shouting out his triumphant message, you might not realize that it takes a minute for the Chicago Bears social media team to edit these up and post for our viewing pleasure. Last week’s Monday Night win in Seattle dropped at 11:53 pm Central Time: Building something special pic.twitter.com/TrvCBNakX1 — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) November 3, 2026 The week before, a Thursday Night Football win against the Patriots dropped at 11:27 p.m. Central Time: Good luck falling asleep after this one pic.twitter.com/YWvaOMGQIr — Chicago Bears (@ChicagoBears) October 23, 2026 That one was a bit earlier and, let’s be honest, victory Fridays are easy to get through – you can catch up on sleep on the weekend. So here we sit again, waiting for the social media team to drop another Good, Better, Best video after the Bears complete the Primetime Trifecta. item.title: Lakers hold off Pistons behind Austin Reaves’ 43 with Luka Dončić out
item.description: Nov 8, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves (15) passes the ball from under the basket against the Detroit Pistons in the second half at Little Caesars Arena. DETROIT — The Lakers had led by 26. By the fourth quarter, that lead was down to one, and the NBA’s leading scorer was on the bench in street clothes. Austin Reaves took it from there. He hit an off-balance 3-pointer with 46 seconds left, waved toward the courtside seats and closed out a season-high 43-point night at the free-throw line as the Lakers beat the Detroit Pistons 121-116 on Sunday at Little Caesars Arena. The Lakers improved to 9-2 with their fifth straight win and are 2-0 without Luka Dončić, who missed his second game of the season with lower back tightness. Reaves went 14 of 27 from the field, made four of six 3-pointers and hit all 11 free throws. He added five rebounds and four assists and committed just one turnover against the NBA’s top-ranked defense. “I thought AR’s decision-making, his aggression, his ability to just consistently touch the paint and get downhill was fantastic tonight,” Lakers coach JJ Redick said. Quentin Grimes scored 10 of his 12 points in the first quarter, when L.A. shot 16 of 23 and built a 38-14 lead. The Lakers stretched it to 40-14 early in the second before Detroit’s bench brought the Pistons back. Daniss Jenkins scored 22 of his career-high 31 points in the first half, including a 3-pointer at the buzzer that cut the deficit to 61-48. Reaves scored 13 in the third quarter, but Detroit closed within three late in the period. The Pistons had a chance to tie it with 9:14 left in the fourth, when Cade Cunningham missed the second of two free throws to leave L.A. ahead 90-89. “We just stayed calm,” Reaves told Spectrum SportsNet. “You can get sped up in those types of moments, but we trust what we got on this team.” Walker Kessler helped rebuild the lead with a huge putback and a free throw to give L.A. an eight point lead with 2:15 left. He finished with 12 points, 16 rebounds and three blocks, while Collin Sexton and Ziaire Williams each scored 17 off the bench. Kevin Huerter added 24 for Detroit, and Cunningham finished with 14 points and eight assists. The Lakers visit the Atlanta Hawks on Monday to close out the back-to-back.

Draped in the boldly bright green and purple of Disney’s District 5 Ducks , Anaheim continued to dive deep into its Bombay chest of offense with Cutter Gauthier's third hat trick in five games and another three power play goals in a 5-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins on Sunday at Honda Center. item.description: Predators celebrate goal against the Wild October 2026 Getty The Nashville Predators are heading into one of their busiest stretches of the season with five away games in eight days. Five consecutive road games will be no easy task for the Preds, but their confidence will be heightened as they continue to play their best hockey of the season. With two days off before the trip begins, the Preds are ready to take their momentum into some tough matchups on the West Coast. The Road Trip Ahead Following two days off, the Preds will travel to California for back-to-back games against Los Angeles and Anaheim on Tuesday and Wednesday. The Friday night matchup against the Golden Knights presents an exciting chance for Nashville to get revenge on the 12-5-2 powerhouse. Having already taken down the Hurricanes, Avalanche (twice), Stars, and Lightning, the Preds have stood toe-to-toe with some of the league’s top teams and will look to claim another victory. The Preds wrap up the road trip against Minnesota the following Tuesday, finally leaving the West Coast to seek revenge against Kirill Kaprizov and the Wild. With five road games in eight days, the Preds couldn’t ask for a better time to travel the coast, looking to keep the game plan simple and ride the momentum of what’s been working. Riding the Momentum After a slow start to the year, the Preds are finding their rhythm with help from both veterans and offseason acquisitions. Among the new acquisitions, it’s been 30-year-old center Ross Colton who has been bringing the heat for the Preds. With a point in three straight games, the new face from the Avs has begun to find his rhythm, recording 3 goals and an assist in his last three games while averaging only 12:48 of ice time per game. As for the veterans, Filip Forsberg and Roman Josi continue to share the puck immaculately, combining for 9 assists during the team’s four-game winning streak. With Josi and Forsberg finding open teammates and the rest of the team capitalizing on those chances, the Preds have found a formula that has worked to win games as of late. While it is unrealistic to expect them to win all five games on their trip, expectations are definitely high as the Preds head to California on Tuesday to face the Kings. item.title: 'We threw it away' - Aston Villa captain John McGinn fumes after twice squandering two-goal lead in 4-4 draw with Manchester United
item.description: Manchester United v Aston Villa FC - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Aston Villa captain John McGinn has criticised his team-mates' game management after they twice surrendered a two-goal cushion in Sunday's chaotic 4-4 draw at Manchester United. Unai Emery's visitors appeared on course for all three points at Old Trafford before conceding twice in stoppage time against their struggling hosts. Scottish midfielder laments costly collapse McGinn admitted the Villans only had themselves to blame after missing the chance to climb the Premier League table against out-of-form United. Strikes from Alysson and Nicolas Jackson inside three minutes and 40 seconds marked the earliest the hosts had trailed 2-0 in the competition. It was also the fastest two-goal away lead since Chelsea managed it after two minutes and 53 seconds at Everton in August 2014. Defensive lapses undermine fast starts Despite their electric opening, Villa allowed Bruno Fernandes to convert a penalty before former team-mate Youri Tielemans equalised in the 44th minute. The away side then restored their two-goal buffer early in the second half when Diogo Dalot fouled Alysson for McGinn to score from the spot in the 48th minute before Leon Goretzka netted five minutes later. Speaking to BBC Match of the Day afterwards, McGinn rued his team's inability to see out either half: "We have to manage these moments better. Not a lot of teams will come here 2-0 and give goals away. "We have to defend better in those positions. In the last 10 minutes of each half, we have to manage better. "We have a lot of inexperienced players but a lot of talent, and that's why we score goals. It doesn't matter if United are low on confidence; you're always up against it." Stoppage-time madness leaves skipper stinging Rather than cruising to victory, the Midlands outfit were undone in added time by substitute Patrick Dorgu, who set up Joshua Zirkzee to make it 4-3 before rising highest to head Fernandes' cross past goalkeeper Zion Suzuki for a dramatic equaliser . Reflecting on that late capitulation and how Emery will react over the hiatus, the Scotland international added: "The third goal was really poor and gave them a lot of encouragement to score. We lost two points. We threw it away. The last five minutes were just madness. It's going to sting. "The manager is a winner; he'll be hurting the way we are. We go play international football, but he'll dwell on it for two weeks." Sunderland clash follows international break With the Premier League now pausing for the November international break, Emery will have a fortnight to address his side's late defensive vulnerabilities before hosting Sunderland on Saturday, November 21 . Securing maximum points at Villa Park will be vital to ensure Sunday's late collapse does not derail their top-half ambitions. Meanwhile, Michael Carrick's relegation-threatened United face a daunting trip to arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield 24 hours later.

item.description: Shedeur Sanders #2 of the Cleveland Browns Getty Former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Bill Cowher sees big potential in a longtime rival’s young quarterback. Cowher shared praise for Cleveland Browns quarterback Shedeur Sanders, who was pressed into action this week after an injury to Deshaun Watson. Sanders performed well despite an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints, but Cowher still sees big things in his future. Steelers Coach Shares Praise for Shedeur Sanders Speaking on the NFL on CBS, Cowher said he believes Sanders should permanently take the starting job from Watson. “Shedeur Sanders should be the starter for this football team. He’s gonna be the future,” Cowher said. “I think what he showed today was his resiliency in coming back. He made great decisions. He extended plays. I love the way he played.” Sanders completed 19-of-31 passes for 297 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday’s 23-22 loss, matching the Saints with a touchdown in overtime before ending the game on a missed two-point conversion pass. Despite the loss, Sanders said afterward that he felt his abilities are growing. “It was cool to even be able to get in that position,” Sanders said . “The moment never felt big, so that’s how I know I’m growing as a quarterback in this league.” Browns head coach Todd Monken said he was proud of the performance from Sanders, but said he would not get into whether he could remain the starter once Watson is able to return from concussion protocol. (Photo by Ryan Sirius Sun/Getty Images) Getty The Los Angeles Chargers entered the season as dark-horse favorites to win the Super Bowl. Then came the 0-8 start that has the entire NFL world in shock. The latest loss came Sunday afternoon against the Houston Texans in a 44-22 final that saw Justin Herbert leave the game with a finger injury. DJ Uiagalelei came on in relief and even threw a touchdown pass, giving fans something to cheer for amid this nightmare start. The extent of Herbert’s injury is unknown at the moment. Chargers reporter Alex Insdorf did share a quote, however, from head coach Jim Harbaugh that noted how the injury “could be a fracture.” Any injury holding Herbert out would be frustrating, yet this situation may allow the Chargers to finally embrace the reality of the team’s 2026 season. Chargers Can Finally Embrace a Tank The Chargers are the NFL’s lone remaining winless team, putting them in line to receive the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. The Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins are in contention as well with one win apiece so far this season. Landing the No. 1 overall pick would give the Chargers options, but a popular prediction is it would allow the team to draft Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. He already looks like an NFL player at the college level and would instantly be Herbert’s top target. The team may also be able to draft him at No. 2 or No. 3 overall as well, depending on how the 2027 quarterback class finishes up this current season. This is not at all what the Chargers expected when the season began. Yet it is the team’s reality and it makes zero sense to put Herbert on the field with any type of injury. The wisest move, given his finger is indeed injured, may be to shut him down for the season and turn to Uiagalelei and Trey Lance once the latter is off injured reserve. That means holding onto Khalil Mack , among many others who could bring back serious value in return. Falling to 0-8 could change the front office’s mind, unless the entire organization believes this season is some sort of massive fluke. What we do know is that Herbert is not going anywhere. On the first night of a back-to-back set on the road, the Los Angeles Lakers decided to sit out Luka Doncic in a clash against one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference, the Detroit Pistons. But in the end, that scarcely mattered. With Doncic out, Austin Reaves took control and popped off for his best game of this season thus far — recording 43 points on 14-of-27 shooting from the field to go along with five rebounds and four assists to lead the Lakers to a 121-116 victory. Reaves was on fire for the entire night, and in the third quarter, he was most certainly feeling himself on one possession in particular. With 6:44 remaining in the period and still 11 seconds left in the shot clock, the Lakers guard decided to hoist an off-balance triple right in Pistons guard Daniss Jenkins and banked in a triple to give him 32 points on the night at that point of the game. The Lakers star knew that that shot wasn’t the ideal one to take with that much time left on the shot clock. Honestly when I stepped back and shot it, I was like, ‘This is some s*** Luka would shoot,” Reaves told reporters after the game, via Dave McMenamin of ESPN.
